item.title: Daily global sea surface ageostrophic current dataset from 1993–2023 via physics-informed deep learning
item.description:
Daily global sea surface ageostrophic current dataset from 1993–2023 via physics-informed deep learning
Guangxi Cui, Ka-Veng Yuen, Ying Chen, Zhiqiang Liu, Dingqi Yang, Guangliang Liu, and Zhongya Cai
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8149–8165, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8149-2026, 2026
Most long-term satellite-based global current datasets capture only large-scale flows driven by pressure differences, missing important nonlinear motions. We used satellite data and a physics-informed deep learning method to create a new global dataset, including these previously missing components. Our currents are more accurate than traditional products, and we show that motions driven by nonlinear effects strongly influence the transport of heat, carbon, and nutrients in ocean.

item.title: Long-term time series of ground-based NDACC FTIR trace gases at Paris between 2011 and 2022
item.description:
Long-term time series of ground-based NDACC FTIR trace gases at Paris between 2011 and 2022
Hao Fu, Pascal Jeseck, Christof Janssen, Corinne Boursier, Christian Rouillé, Patrick Marie-Jeanne, Julien Rozé, Tamer Abou Karroum, and Yao Té
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-762,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We present a dataset of ten atmospheric gases above Paris, with records spanning up to 12 years between 2011 to 2022. The gases are measured using a ground-based infrared instrument. We describe the data processing and assess the uncertainties. Methane and nitrous oxide increase, while several other gases decrease. The data can be used to study atmospheric changes above a major city and to check satellite measurements.
